title: Reverse cost-model direction: raise random_page_cost 1.5->3.0, seq_page_cost 0.8->1.0
configuration_cause: GetUserTweets consumes 87.6% of terminal capacity at p50 138us; the incumbent's cache-optimistic cost model (random_page_cost 1.5, seq_page_cost 0.8) was set by the refuted r007 direction, and the r008 upward reversal was never executed. Cost-model calibration is the only in-scope lever that can change the GetUserTweets access path without touching WAL or predicate locks.
mechanism: GetUserTweets dominates terminal time (87.6% capacity, p50 138us, p95 200us). The incumbent cost model is cache-optimistic (random_page_cost 1.5, seq_page_cost 0.8), a direction already refuted at r007. Raising random_page_cost to 3.0 and seq_page_cost to 1.0 (PostgreSQL defaults) re-prices random index probes relative to sequential scans, so the planner may pick a cheaper path for the skewed user_id lookup and shrink pages touched per call. This is a bounded reversal of a falsified direction, not a replay of the WAL bundle.
query_effect: GetUserTweets is a single-table lookup by user_id; raising random_page_cost makes the planner prefer a sequential or bitmap path when the index probe is estimated expensive, potentially reducing per-call page touches for skewed users.
expected_tps_effect: Small increase (>=0.3%) if the access path improves; unchanged if the plan is already optimal.
expected_latency_effect: GetUserTweets p50/p95 decrease by >=1% if the path changes; unchanged otherwise.

predictions.rationale: Re-priced random reads may select a cheaper path for the dominant lookup.
Tail follows the same path change; p95 200us has headroom.
Freed terminal capacity from the 87.6% dominant transaction raises completed TPS.

alternatives.statement: If the planner already uses the optimal Index Scan for GetUserTweets, the cost-model change leaves the plan and latency unchanged, and TPS stays flat.
If WAL sync (0.11ms average) rather than query path limits throughput, GetUserTweets latency is unchanged and only WAL knobs would move TPS.

why_exceeds_incumbent: The incumbent's cost model is cache-optimistic from a refuted direction; restoring PostgreSQL-default costs is a bounded, untested reversal that can only help if the GetUserTweets plan is suboptimal, and is neutral otherwise.

nodes.label: Re-priced random vs sequential reads may select cheaper GetUserTweets path

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Raise from incumbent 1.5 toward PostgreSQL default 4.0; 3.0 is within safe [1.0,6.0] and is a larger amplitude than the untested r008 value 2.5, reversing the refuted r007 direction (1.5->1.1).
knob_changes.mechanism_role: planner cost of random/cached reads; raising it discourages random index probes

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Raise from 0.8 to PostgreSQL default 1.0, within safe [0.5,2.0]; paired with random_page_cost to keep the random/seq ratio at 3.0.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: I/O cost scale paired with random_page_cost; raising it rebalances toward sequential paths
